data.title: Excavation at the Šimunky hillfort in Dolná Mariková
data.excerpt: Over one weekend the Hradiská civic association, working with the Trenčín Museum, carried out an archaeological excavation at Šimunky on the Široká crag in Dolná Mariková, where an important fortification of our Slavic ancestors stood in the time of Great Moravia. Two Great Moravian hoes, an excellently preserved house key, knives, arrowheads and Púchov culture pottery were among the finds rescued.
data.metaTitle: Excavation at the Šimunky hillfort (Dolná Mariková)
data.metaDescription: In May 2016 the Hradiská civic association and the Trenčín Museum excavated the Great Moravian hillfort of Šimunky on the Široká crag in Dolná Mariková.

children.text: Over the weekend our Hradiská civic association, in cooperation with the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín, carried out an archaeological excavation in Dolná Mariková on the Široká crag, in the part called Šimunky, where an important fortification of our Slavic ancestors stood in the time of Great Moravia.

At the end of the 1990s Mr Gašpar Zemančík discovered the first finds of the Great Moravian period at Šimunky. The first surface collection on the fortification was then carried out by the Archaeological Circle from Považská Bystrica under the direction of the archaeologist Jozef Moravčík, during which a great number of unique finds were rescued. Since that time, however, no archaeological excavation has been carried out on the fortification, and the site has been afflicted by raids of looters with metal detectors. Our aim was therefore to organise an excavation of the area of the fortification, aimed at rescuing the metal finds and at documenting life at the hillfort in the Early Middle Ages, and possibly also in earlier periods, which have so far been demonstrated on the fortification only by a small number of finds.

blocks.caption: Šimunky – a view of the hillfort
blocks.alt: Šimunky – a view of the hillfort

children.text: We asked the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín for cooperation, and its director Peter Martinisko met us fully halfway and was delighted by the idea of the museum working with our association. The museum’s archaeologist Mgr Peter Schreiber is concerned, among other things, with research into the occupation of the north-western Váh region, and in particular of the area of the Púchov and Považská Bystrica districts, and so he too was very well disposed towards the idea of carrying out an excavation at the hillfort in Dolná Mariková.

The first step we took was to clear the hillfort of self-seeded trees and dense scrub. A year earlier the area of the hillfort had been all but impenetrable. The association devoted one weekend to the clearing. One of our members, however, had already cleared a large part of it beforehand. We then gradually obtained the consent of the owners of the plots on which the hillfort lay. For every excavation the owner of the land has to give consent. The Trenčín Museum drew up a project for the excavation, and this was approved for us by the Regional Monuments Board in Trenčín, which also laid down the precise conditions of the excavation.

blocks.caption: The cleared acropolis awaits the excavators
blocks.alt: The cleared acropolis awaits the excavators

children.text:
Once we had dealt with all the necessary formalities and preparations, we were only waiting for a weekend with suitable weather that would also suit most of us in terms of timing. After several postponements of the excavation (for objective reasons), D-Day then came – or rather two D-Days – the weekend of 7–8 May 2016, when the excavation could begin. It turned out to be the right choice, because the weather was positively ideal for an excavation. Besides the members of our association, the invitation to the excavation was also accepted by former members of the archaeological circle, Mr Štefan Meliš (at the age of 88 a living legend), the discoverer of the hillfort Gašpar Zemančík and Mr Ladislav Janech. 
 
 Over the course of 2 days we dug one trench measuring 1 × 2 metres, and in addition every metal find located with the metal detectors was documented by a small trench measuring 40 × 40 cm. The trenches made in this way were then professionally surveyed by the skilful surveyors from the firm
, who went out of their way to help us, waited patiently for all the trenches to be dug and surveyed them with professional precision. They deserve our enormous thanks.

children.text: And so what is the result? What did we find? I think we can all be more than satisfied with the outcome. Evidently thanks to the dense growth mentioned above, which covered the hillfort in past years, some parts of the hillfort had not been plundered by the raids of looters as badly as we had feared. We found several early medieval knives, arrowheads, mounts, bucket attachments and other smaller metal finds. From our point of view the most wonderful finds were two hoes of the Great Moravian period, one of which is preserved in such good condition that one could dig a field with it without any difficulty even today. Another find that is quite literally top-class, of a kind I do not have documented in many other places in Slovakia, is an excellently preserved house key, likewise probably of the Great Moravian period. I shall also mention a fragment of a riding spur. Among the finds that we assign to the period of the turn of the eras (the Púchov culture), I can mention a quantity of thick-walled pottery with typical Celtic decoration and a piece of flint that may have served as part of a fire-steel set.

blocks.caption: Cleaning up the micro-trenches from the detector finds
blocks.alt: Cleaning up the micro-trenches from the detector finds

children.text: Our excavation demonstrated that Šimunky was occupied at least in the period of the Púchov culture, and that the most intensive occupation was precisely that by our Slavic ancestors in the period of the 9th/10th century. We managed to rescue a quantity of metal finds that sooner or later might have become a trophy, or merely an article of trade, for looters. We have thus enriched the history of Slovakia, and of Dolná Mariková in particular, with new insights into the importance of the occupation in the period of Great Moravia and at the turn of the eras. We searched the area of the hillfort with a larger number of detectors so intensively that it will no longer be of interest to looters.

At the same time it turned out that intensive cooperation between us as amateur enthusiasts and the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín can bring very good results, both from the scholarly and from the lay point of view.

We thank all those who took part for their help, and especially those who came to the excavation from greater distances. Above all, our thanks go to the management of the Trenčín Museum in Trenčín for their helpfulness. We also thank the mayor, Ing. Peter Šujak, for his cooperation in organising the excavation, and likewise the owners of the land, Mrs Š. Martausová-Trúchlá and Mr Bakala and Mr F. Martaus, for meeting us halfway and understanding the importance of the excavation. 
 
 And one surprising thing to finish with. In our discussion group on Facebook I announced that over the weekend we would be doing an archaeological excavation and that anyone who had a detector could come and help us. Nobody came. 
 
 Orgoň.
